units.translation: The particle τοι with ἄν coalesces into one long syllable τἄν by crasis, which is neglected in the manuscripts, where τ᾽ ἄν is consistently written, as in the places cited above Pr. 395 [Sept. 552]. Ag. 870 [Ch. 1003]. Eum. 888. In the same way τοι and ἄρα coalesce into τἄρα, of which there are several examples in other authors, one in Aeschylus fr. 328.
where M has τοίνυν, but correctly τοί νιν is written in one Parisian apograph.
where Hermann reads λέγω 'γώ.
where correctly εἴ is written above in the Florentine apograph, and τοι was changed to τι by Hermann.
Thus in the scholia on Homer Il. 23, 10: in other authors οἵ τε, or οἱ δέ, or οἱ γάρ.
Thus I wrote for ταῦτα τοῖς, which is in M with the article uselessly added, which is not added at v. 757 τοιάδ᾽ ἐξ ἀνδρῶν ὀνείδη πολλάκις κλύων κακῶν -.
For such a sin as this they must pay the penalty to the gods.
By such woes, I tell you, I am bowed down.
But the winged hound of Zeus, I tell you, will rend the great rag of your body.
To me, who know, he has shouted these tidings.
But you, I tell you, be mindful of the city's rites that love sacrifice.
I tremble before heavy fortune, I tell you.
The scout, I tell you, brings us some news.
For the bearer of this boastful sign, I tell you, it would rightly and justly be a fitting name.
Sharpened as I am, I tell you, you will not blunt me with words.
You, I tell you, know her (Fate) as she crosses.
Terrible things, I tell you, you say.
It is possible, I tell you, to remember.
But he prospered, I tell you, who soonest broke off the breath of life.
I will send, I tell you, even a lament for all.
I am drenched, I tell you.
I will send you, I tell you, with ill-sounding laments.
Such, I tell you, are the customs of the torch-bearers (thus Schuetz for τοιοίδ᾽ ἕτοιμοι).
Such things, I tell you, you hear from me, a woman.
I revere Zeus, I tell you, the great god of strangers.
From these, I tell you, the child is not present here.
With such words, I tell you, I deem it right to address him.
But may you care, I tell you, for what you intend to accomplish.
For they say, I tell you, that the son of Alcmena once was sold and endured to get a slave's barley-cake.
Speaking to you, I tell you, she ceases her clear speech.
For he is thus, but she, I tell you, lies as the lover of this man.
But if, I tell you, there should be enough of these toils –.
A double-mourning dirge, I tell you, laments you at the tomb.
You, I tell you, I address.
I judge, I tell you, that he should be held fast.
He must, I tell you, die by violence.
You, I tell you, will kill yourself, not I.
From these, I tell you, confusion falls upon my mind.
This, I tell you, is the third storm that has been accomplished upon the royal house.
Zeus, I tell you, reveres this reverence of the lawless.
Such, I tell you, is the reverence we justly fear.
You, I tell you, destroyed the ancient allotment and deceived the ancient goddesses with wine.
You, I tell you, soon – my arrow.
Deprived of my fatherland, you, I tell you, settled me.
873 I breathe, I tell you, with fury.
I rejoice, I tell you, that these things are being accomplished favorably for my land.
Everywhere, I tell you, it blazes.
You, I tell you, are the city, and you the people.
If, I tell you, the sons of Aegyptus have power over you.
You must, I tell you, flee.
But I mark out for you a device under the stars.
There is need, I tell you, of deep thought for safety.
